A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AIScene study. All ten pages of each were inspected, including readable equations, seven figures, four tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original AIScene segmentation experiments on SemanticKITTI and nuScenes, component and backbone ablations in Tables 2–4, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and ablations, with revised AIScene nuScenes results in Table 1.

M1.justification: The teacher–student framework, point erasure, MixPatch, InsFill, pool operations, and training objectives remain unchanged. The five-point pool filter explained in v3 was already specified in v2 Section 4.2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate driving-scene LiDAR semantic segmentation on SemanticKITTI with 19 classes and nuScenes with 16 classes. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparators, including both LaserMix representations, DDSemi, and LASS3D. Figure 6(c) also retains the same augmentation comparisons, including CylinderMix. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 specifies the confidence threshold only as the same setting as LaserMix; v3 explicitly reports 0.9 and describes it as experimentally satisfactory. The supplied PDFs do not establish whether this changes the threshold or merely documents its value. Splits, metrics, backbones, and other stated settings match.

E4.justification: The backbone and component ablations, dual-scene versus multi-scene comparison, erasure analysis, mixing-strategy comparison, patch-count sensitivity, and qualitative examples are retained. The added threshold explanation supplies no new ablation or sensitivity results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or statistical significance tests. Figure 7 retains the same model class probabilities; these are not newly added statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises AIScene's nuScenes mIoU at 1%, 10%, and 50% labeled data from 63.4, 73.7, and 76.3 to 60.2, 72.3, and 76.4; the 20% result remains 75.0. The reported average changes from 72.1 to 70.9, reducing the average advantage over DDSemi from 2.4 to 1.2 points and the 1% advantage from 5.3 to 2.1 points. This substantially reduces the headline effect on a primary benchmark, although rankings, SemanticKITTI results, and ablation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations (1)–(10), covering EMA, erasure, patch pools, mixing, and losses, are unchanged. The added sparse-patch rationale is informal explanation, not a new assumption, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the quantified nuScenes superiority claim: the 1% gain changes from 5.3 to 2.1 points, and the introduction's average gain changes from 2.4 to 1.2 points. The core methodological contributions and state-of-the-art positioning remain; the conclusion drops its additional emphasis on remarkable gains in the most challenging settings.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 replaces the brief claim that pool filtering ensures semantic diversity with an explanation that patches or instances containing fewer than five points have uncertain spatial structure, creating semantic ambiguity and augmentation noise. Other mechanism interpretations and applicability discussions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 first states the numerical confidence threshold, 0.9, instead of referring readers to LaserMix. The abstract adds a repository location for a future code release, without establishing that code is available. The five-point minimum is relocated from Section 4.2 to Section 3.3; hardware, framework, loss weights, and patch-count details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Hierarchical Supervision and Shuffle Data Augmentation for 3D Semi-Supervised Object Detection and SSDA3D in its augmentation overview. The surrounding research positioning remains unchanged; most other citation changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to pool-filtering and implementation explanations, numerical headline statements, and the conclusion. v3 also updates affiliations and author-credit notes, adds acknowledgments, and corrects a table-caption typo. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The same seven figures and four tables remain. Figure 6(c)'s caption explicitly names SemanticKITTI, Figure 7 receives slight formatting changes, and figure/caption spacing is tightened. Text reflow brings the entire conclusion onto page 8 rather than continuing onto page 9.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves self-contained documentation by explicitly stating the confidence threshold, explaining the existing five-point filter, and identifying a planned code-release location. The revised nuScenes margins are reflected consistently in the headline text, but their unexplained cause limits conclusions about improved empirical reliability. The supported quality gain is therefore limited to clearer documentation and explanation.
